changes: Reuse at most two lazy native context workers. Eight sequential qualified fixture jobs use one Rust thread identity instead of eight; after two blocked deliveries, later work reuses a worker.

Keep the existing two-job limit across queued work, evaluation and response delivery. No worker starts for an unused/off lane. Idle workers retire after one second; close wakes them and the original two-second drain includes their retirement.

Keep exact request binding, strict evaluation, native busy refusals and independent hook workers. Failed spawns and a lost last worker release unevaluated reservations without replay; delivery panic does not discard the reusable worker.
Recheck the existing four-second accepted-request budget immediately before evaluation. This neither extends native nor SDK/client deadlines.

Serialize seven notification unit fixtures that observe a process-wide global-loss counter, including the fixture that deliberately advances it. Preserve all prior assertions and add unrelated-scope invalidation after global loss. Production notifier bytes remain unchanged.
